newsitem.title: FRANCE: TPS in MGM audio visual rights deal.
newsitem.headline: TPS in MGM audio visual rights deal.

text.p: French digital satellite television joint-venture TPS has signed a five-year audio-visual rights deal with U.S. studio Metro-Goldwyn Mayer, TF1 Chairman Patrick Le Lay said.
TF1, controlled by Bouygues, is France's biggest private broadcaster and a major partner in the Television Par Satellite (TPS) venture with state-owned France Television, M6 and Lyonnaise des Eaux.
TPS will start services at the end of 1996 in competition with digital satellite pay television channel Canal Satellite.
"We signed a deal with MGM," Le Lay told a news conference during the MIPCOM television industry meeting here.
He added TPS had signed a deal with Paramount last week.
"It's nice to be backed by such majors," he said.
Le Lay gave no financial details, nor was it clear whether the TPS audio visual rights would prevent Canal Satellite for signing up MGM and Paramount for pay-television rights in France.
